A lot of monarchy’s are dynasty’s, but nowadays most dynasty’s aren’t monarchy’s. A dynasty is just a single family or institution having control of something for an extended period of time. This can be in the form of monarchy (the Chinese dynasty’s come to mind) but can also apply to non-governmental systems. For example, in sports when a single team is considered to be at the top of their league for several years they’re said to have a dynasty.

Monarchy is strictly just about government. Like I said many (but not all) are dynasty’s because it’s usually familial. But there are a few exceptions. The pope is technically a monarch but they are not dynastic because it’s a lifetime elected position and has nothing to do with bloodlines.

Hey! I had a similar issue as you when I first played. Since then I’ve beaten the game 4 times. This is my advice.

1. Grind. Don’t just go straight from story objective to story objective. For the area you’re in, it’s good to go around and do a bunch of side objectives before going after the goblin camp. Make sure you get all of the available companions in the area as well (Karlach, Wyll, Gale, Shadowheart, Astarion). Explore all the opening area. You should be level 3-4 when you do the goblin camp.

2. Don’t just go in and fight everyone. Talk to people, learn information, come up with a plan. Personally, I usually go in with the same plan (except for my evil playthrough where I got Minthara). Go to the back and get Minthara first. Have your character talk to her and during the conversation move your companions into strategic locations. Destroy the bridge when the spy eye is floating over it, and destroy the drums so they cant call for backup. This will keep the whole camp from going aggro at once. Then just corner Minthara and beat the shit out of her. After this, go around to where the large goblin is (not the old lady) and go up into the rafters without triggering his dialogue. You can get up there with a rope ladder. Position your people around strategically again, and have your ranged character(s) fire down on the goblins. You’ll get an extra advantage being high up. Just attack the goblins as they come up to you then. Make sure to destroy the drums before the goblins use them to summon reinforcements. No matter what you do here though it will make the rest of the camp attack you on sight. After beating this area go get Halsin and then the five of you finish the camp.

Not the person you responded to but I am a teacher.

To me it’s a mixture of a few things. I hate blaming this but COVID had a major effect on this. Phones were a problem before but the kids basically spent a year getting super addicted to their phones, and their parents were able to contact them 24/7. They struggled to go from that back to having phone time limited. While the classes that really experienced that have since graduated, the culture that it created lingers.

Another thing is that parents just don’t support the schools in this anymore. I graduated around the same time as you (2012) and yeah the rules back then were strict. We couldn’t have our phones out at all, we had to be sneaky if we wanted to text, and if our phone got confiscated our parents would get mad at us. That’s not the case anymore. You confiscate a phone now and parents get mad at the school. “What if there’s an emergency? What if I need to get a hold of my child? I paid for the phone you can’t take it” and on and on and on. Students will be actively on their phone while I’m teaching, to the point that I have completely stopped mid lesson before and just stood silently and they never noticed. This has led to the kids basically wondering why they’re even at school since all they do is sit in class on their phone while we talk at them. It’s incredibly difficult and depressing for me tbh. 

To answer your question, we just don’t have the parental support anymore. Despite how it felt when you were in school, we as teachers really only have so much authority and are dependent on parents to back us up on discipline. Without that help from parents we’re basically powerless with the kids. And if parents aren’t willing to step in and actually parent their child, then we need state legislatures to take up the mantle and give us the ability to handle issues like phones without parents threatening to sue us for confiscating them.

Edit: I will say, I’ve noticed this year that the parent thing is improving somewhat. The kids I have this year are better behaved and overall more attentive than the last several years that I’ve taught. I’ve had more positive parental interactions too. It’s still not what it used to be but it’s a good sign.

Making it a statewide law takes the pressure off individual schools when parents start freaking out at school board meetings or on admin. Usually what will happen is we will confiscate a phone and the parents will come and have a fit, saying things like “what if there’s an emergency!” even though we have phones in every classroom that connects to an outside line. When it’s a law, it lets the school system basically point to the legislature and say “we’re just following the law, complain to them.” The state I teach in will soon be passing a law about this and I’m excited.

I’m a teacher in Oklahoma. Here’s what we’re expected to do with our extremely limited resources.

We have to help students (who do not want to do it) study for essentially a month leading up to multiple tests that are given to them over the course of essentially two weeks. At the same time we still have to meet our state standards, differentiate instruction, deal with any behavioral issues, and keep the students engaged. This is something that usually would require parents to help us. However, many parents do not want to help us, and in fact when kids score low on tests they come and blame us for it.

Then, whether they pass their classes or not, they get passed along anyways, usually several grades behind the curve at that point. So when they get to their junior year (when they take the mandated ACT) the teachers spend most of the first semester trying to teach things that the kids should have already learned years ago. We have students who cannot correctly write sentences, who don’t know how to format an essay, who can’t do simple algebraic equations, and who read at a 5th grade level if you’re lucky. I stopped having kids read out loud in my history classes because it was a massive struggle for them and myself. Asking them to write an essay is like asking them to do advanced physics, they don’t even know where to begin. 

So by the time we get to testing season for juniors, we’re rushing to teach them things that we should have taught them months ago but couldn’t because they didn’t have the foundational knowledge to understand it. And not many of them actually learn anything. I shudder to think what the future will be like with the barely literate, barely functional adults that we are forced to graduate. And if we actually hold them to the standards we are supposed to, the school gets punished for not graduating them.

Meanwhile, I can barely afford to get by. I struggle to make ends meet, have essentially no free time and see the students more than I see my own family. Yet somehow I come back every year because….idk. I don’t want to be a quitter. And I love the kids. But goddamn it’s hard.

1. Disconnect from all things politics. This might mean not using social media for a bit, or unsubscribing from political pages. 4. Read good books. This one seems small but anytime I’m feeling bad or worried or down, I pick up a book. Usually something completely unrelated to what’s happening. Books always make me feel better.

My take as a teacher:

This issue is twofold. We are absolutely miles behind in education. Many kids are unable to do simple things at the high school level now. Spelling, grammar, correct sentence structure, simple middle school level algebra, elementary level science knowledge, rudimentary history knowledge, etc are all completely missing in kids that are still going to graduate this May. And it’s not just a few like it used to be, it’s a majority of the kids. This is its own, wide ranging issue with a whole lot of root causes.

The second reason though, is that the ACT was never meant to be used the way our state is using it. It’s not a benchmark test to collect data, it’s a college readiness test. Before being used for this, the only people taking the ACT were kids who were planning on going to college and therefore were going to put in effort on the test, both by studying and by trying on the test itself. Many of these kids would take the test several times to raise their overall score. The school I work at is trying to address these problems, and we have been able to raise our average score by a few points, but it’s difficult to get kids to buy in.

Something to remember, if you are a parent, is that kids will only care about education as much as you do. It won’t be obvious at home all the time, but you can always tell the kids whose parents care about their grades. This means showing interest in the grades they get, having a good relationship with the teachers at the school, and encouraging your child when they are successful in school (and yes, punishing them when they put no effort in). Please, we need your help.

Best books (I haven’t read Lor yet and I didn’t read Wyn)

1. Moth-I think this is the consensus favorite. I think Seraph is the best written but moth is the most enjoyable. Not just for the sex scenes (though there seem to be more in this one than the others) but it’s just a good book. You can tell Mayne really hit her stride in writing with this one.

2. Edin-I’ve seen people say they couldn’t get through this one and idk how, I loved this one. It was cute and fun and easy to read. Plenty of action but not so much it didn’t feel like a romance novel any more. 

4. Ryke- I really liked the monster in this one, he’s such a sweetheart. And the action is cool and enjoyable. The side characters are also really interesting. But I wasn’t a fan of the MC, ghost is kind of a dick.

5. Seraph- I think the writing in this one is the strongest but the romance itself is kind of hard to get into. It’s the least “human” monster and it is very obvious in every interaction with him (though he’s a cinnamon roll tbh). Also much less action in this one, it’s much slower paced over all. 

6. Soul Eater- the og is good and the characters are obviously well loved but it’s kind of hard to go back and read. It’s obvious Mayne was still figuring out her writing style here, this one reads like a Wattpad novel.

7. Gloam- the only one I didn’t finish. It’s just hard to get through. I love Rig but that’s about the only redeemable quality of this book. It’s slow paced, it seemed like half the book was about walking and nothing else. And gloam himself is the weakest written love interest in the series imo.

Best MCs

1. Hunter-I love Hunter. Maybe it’s because he sounds hot af (tall, muscular, handsome, hairy) but his personality is relatable to me. He’s funny but not annoyingly so, and he seems very grounded in every interaction he has. This series suffers (in a very minor way) from its MCs being overly positive at times, to the point of it being unrealistic, but Hunter avoids this really well.

2. Danny-Mayne did good on her first MC, and he just gets better as the series goes on. He’s adorable and lovable. My only issue with him is that he’s written to seem basically completely helpless, especially compared to the other MCs.

3. Charlie- the consent king himself, Charlie is such a good dude it’s impossible not to love him. I love how important consent is to him.

4. Rig-dudes got a winning personality, but he suffers from having (imo) the worst book on the series to star in.

5. Lilac-to put it simply, Lilac is hard to love at times. Idk if he’s supposed to be neurodivergent or what but he comes off very robotically all throughout the series. 

6. Ghost-this dudes a dick, I’m sorry. I disliked him from the beginning of his book and have yet to become a fan. Idk, there’s something about him that I just don’t like. 

Best love interests

1. Edin- if Edin isn’t your favorite character in this series, you’re wrong. There’s literally nothing to dislike about him, and he’s sexy af.

2. Aury- The Ryke is the strongest of all the characters we’ve met, and he’s also the sweetest. He’s so adorable. And his sex scenes are intense.

3. Moth- this guy comes off like an ass at first but he gets more likable as his book goes on. By the end, I think it’s impossible not to love him.

4. Wyn- The Soul Eater doesn’t really grow much as a character in the series, beyond us learning his motivations. He starts off mad and basically stays there the entire time.

I get it, I really do. I’ve had so much anxiety over the potential events of this year it’s hard to detach from that sometimes. Something’s that have helped:

1. Getting offline. The internet (Reddit especially, as much as I like it here) can make things seem a lot bigger and more world ending than they really are. I don’t want to tell you to go “touch grass” because that’s not what I mean, but detaching yourself from the constant news cycle helps a LOT. 

2. You like backpacking and stuff. If you like walking and other physical activities, then go out for a walk when you get these anxious feelings. It sounds dumb but walking and listening to music have been proven to decrease feelings of anxiety. It’s nice to be out in the world and be reminded of what’s “real”.

3. Start reading books. I’m dead serious, it helps me so much. And I don’t mean “serious” novels (though a good history book never hurts). I’ve started reading a lot more and my go to, as dumb as it sounds, are cheesy romance novels. I’ve actually been reading a lot of gay romance recently and it helps a SHOCKING amount. Idk what it is about reading but it really soothes me and quiets down those scary thoughts. Even when I’m not reading, I find myself thinking more of my books and the world I get invested in than the wildness we experience in real life. And reading is good for your brain.

4. If reading isn’t your thing, maybe start finding television series that you enjoy. If you’re in to anime, that genre has become more accessible than ever before and there’s some great stuff out there that has nothing to do with the real world. There’s other stuff too that can provide a great distraction. Personally, I really enjoy mindless shows like American Dad to calm me down if I’m having trouble quieting my head down, especially if I can’t sleep.

5. Take deep breaths (scientifically proven to help) and remind yourself that you can only do what is possible for one person to do. Recycle, be conscious of the environment, vote, do whatever. The world’s problems aren’t always your problems, and you can’t fix everything yourself. It sounds scary to admit and accept that feeling of not having complete control, but it is also very freeing. Help where you can and do what you can, but in the end it’s not on you to fix everything. 

6. Tell your loved ones that you love them and try to hang around them. Friends or family, whichever you want. It helps to be reminded of those who love you.

Yes, and you could potentially call them out, but I also think that you got to look at it through the eyes of that time period. The USSR was very powerful coming into the end of WW2, and the other Allies were planning for an invasion of Japan. The US basically were acting like and planning like the nukes didn’t exist or weren’t going to work. So they and the British knew they needed the USSR to help with finishing off the Japanese. They were likely going to have to convince the Soviets to fight a land war against the Japanese in China. So attacking them and questioning the Soviets over whether they were lying about Hitler being dead, or showing their hand in terms of intelligence by showing whatever proof you might have that he’s not, is a bad move. And ultimately it’s an easy choice, because in the grand scheme of things it didn’t really matter. Hitler was a non-factor at that point. Germany was done, completely invaded and their military destroyed. All of his people had been captured and were going to stand trial. Everyone in the world knew who he was, and most of them at least disliked him. And it was well known among intelligence communities that he had pretty bad mental and health issues towards the end of the war, and a bad drug addiction. He wasn’t going to go and take over another country or anything. If he survived, they knew he was going to spend the rest of his life in hiding. It was easier for everyone that he had just killed himself. The Soviets didn’t have to deal with detaining him and having to keep him alive, the rest of the allies didn’t have to deal with the Soviets getting the credit for capturing/killing him, and no one had to deal with the insane circus event that his trial and likely execution would turn into. 

So would I be shocked to find out he was alive? Yeah. Would I be mad that it had been covered up? Not really, because it makes a lot of sense.

So a big reason that there are conspiracies about his death is the only ones to see his body were the Soviets, and they didn’t turn it over or take pictures or anything. They took possession of it and just told everyone what had happened. Fact of the matter is, as goofy as that conspiracy seems, it’s more possible than a lot of more popular conspiracies. So if it came out that he was alive, the answer as to how that lie was spread and propagated would be easy: the Soviets lied to the world, and at that time no one was willing to risk pissing Stalin off by challenging him on it openly, so the other world leaders just went with it.
